cases.title: Positive reference-layer source set
cases.notes: Synthetic reference primitives. V4 is not applicable: the fixture carries no real semantics or governance and is non-normative.

cases.title: Positive semantic-layer source set referencing reference tokens
cases.notes: References reference-layer tokens via {group.token}; resolution succeeds only within the declared graph (see manifest fixture).

cases.title: Positive component-layer source set binding semantic tokens
cases.notes: Binds a semantic token; never references the reference layer directly.

cases.title: Positive product-profile source set overriding an approved test extension point
cases.notes: Overrides only the approved test extension point declared in the manifest; grants no real Product-Profile acceptance.

cases.title: Positive source-set manifest
cases.notes: A Source-Set Manifest is a CDS-owned document, not a DTCG token document, so V2 (DTCG token/color/resolver) is not applicable. Declares all four source sets, a consistent dependency graph, the resolver, and the product-profile boundary.

cases.title: Positive resolver document with explicit ordered composition
cases.notes: Explicit, reproducible ordered composition over locally declared source sets using $ref and RFC 6901 JSON Pointer; local-only. The resolved output is generated and non-normative.

cases.title: Positive integrated composition of all four source sets via manifest and resolver
cases.notes: The whole declared graph resolves downward without cycles or undeclared references. V4 remains not applicable: synthetic, non-normative artifacts confer no Candidate or Stable status.

cases.title: Negative: duplicate object member name
cases.notes: Duplicate member `alpha`. Fails V1 and is not repaired via first-key-wins or last-key-wins; later layers are not assessed. JSON Schema alone cannot reliably detect this — a duplicate-key-aware parser is required.

cases.title: Negative: dangling token reference
cases.notes: Structurally well-formed; the referenced token does not exist, so reference resolution fails at V2.

cases.title: Negative: cross-file reference cycle
cases.notes: Fixture A references B and B references A, forming a cycle. Both files are structurally valid; resolution fails at V2.

cases.title: Negative: prohibited backward layer dependency in a manifest
cases.notes: A reference-layer source set declares a dependency on a semantic-layer source set (upward). The manifest is structurally valid (V1) and not a DTCG token document (V2 N/A); the direction violation fails at V3. The declarative token paths in this negative manifest are intentionally not materialized; the case tests graph direction, not file existence.

cases.title: Negative: incompatible referenced type
cases.notes: A number-typed token references a string-typed token; the type incompatibility fails at V2.

cases.title: Negative: undeclared cross-file reference
cases.notes: References a source set not declared in the manifest/resolver graph. The alias is syntactically valid (V2), but the reference leaves the declared graph and fails closed at V3.

cases.title: Negative: invalid or absent CDS extension namespace
cases.primaryFailureReason: old or unknown CDS namespace / missing profileVersion
cases.notes: Uses the old `cds` key (a foreign extension, preserved but not normative) instead of `io.github.kaykaspers.cds`, and lacks profileVersion; the CDS source-set identity requirement fails at V3 (the token-document schema requires the CDS namespace at the document root).

cases.title: Negative: unreleased/preview DTCG feature
cases.notes: Uses a token $type that the pinned DTCG 2025.10 reports do not define (a stand-in for a preview/draft feature). Only pinned-stable features are authoritative; the preview feature fails at V2.

cases.title: Positive: valid Semantic Status vocabulary
cases.notes: Complete authorized vocabulary: 5 axes, 25 tokens, unknown everywhere, path/value agreement. The objective semantic-status V4 checks run despite the testOnly/nonNormative fixture flags and pass; non-objective V4 aspects stay visible as an informational limitation.

cases.title: Negative: missing authorized status axis
cases.notes: The evidence axis is entirely absent. Primary failure: missing authorized axis (V4). Secondary: token count 20 != 25 (semantic-status-count) is documented, not the primary result.

cases.title: Negative: missing explicit unknown value
cases.notes: The condition axis lacks `unknown`. Primary failure: unknown must exist explicitly on every axis and is never an omitted default (V4). Secondary: token count 24 != 25.

cases.title: Negative: unauthorized extra status axis
cases.notes: Adds an unauthorized axis `trend`. Primary failure: the axis set is fixed to condition/severity/confidence/freshness/evidence (V4). Secondary: token count 26 != 25.

cases.title: Negative: unauthorized extra status value
cases.notes: Adds an unauthorized value `perfect` on the condition axis. Primary failure: the per-axis value set is fixed (V4). Secondary: token count 26 != 25.

cases.title: Negative: token path and value disagree
cases.primaryFailureReason: token path and technical value identifier disagree
cases.notes: status.condition.nominal carries the value 'degraded'. Primary failure: the token value must preserve its stable technical value identifier (V4).

cases.title: Negative: aggregate status role
cases.notes: Introduces status.health.overall. Primary failure: no aggregated health role may exist (V4). Secondary: token count 26 != 25.

cases.title: Negative: visual role leakage into status semantics
cases.notes: Adds an appearance-oriented value `icon` on the condition axis. Primary failure: status meaning is non-visual; visual roles may not enter the semantic vocabulary (V4). Secondary: token count 26 != 25.

cases.title: Negative: case-only identifier collision
cases.notes: status.condition.nominal carries the value 'Nominal', colliding with its technical identifier by case only. Primary failure: case-only identifier collisions fail closed (V4). Key-level case collisions are additionally blocked structurally by the token-document schema at V3 and are unit-tested against the checker directly.
